intro: Five forced choices. You land on one operating tension — and the orgs that already live that bet.

questions.prompt: Who should own the product craft day to day?

a.label: Engineers own problem, priority, and ship — strategy fights live in grooming

b.label: A PM owns the product surface; engineering delivers against that bet

questions.prompt: What is a PM for in your org?

a.label: Delete the role if it doesn’t create unique value — technical leads hold the loop

b.label: Each PM owns a P&L metric end-to-end, like a mini business unit

questions.prompt: At scale, how do you keep the product coherent?

a.label: Mission swarms and radical autonomy — hierarchy is the bottleneck

b.label: Pull strategy up — VP-centered bets beat squad freedom that frays the experience

questions.prompt: What should you ship as the product?

a.label: Durable API primitives others compose — hide the protocol complexity

b.label: An agent OS that takes the action end-to-end — not a suggestion layer

a.label: Skip CEO and sales gates — autonomy is the operating system

b.label: Pick explore / expand / extract methods by lifecycle stage — process matches maturity
